        - paragraph: In simple English
        - heading "Understand Tangent Line" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "A tangent line touches a curve locally and has slope equal to the derivative at the point. In Tangent Line, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is Tangent line: y-f(a)=f'(a)(x-a). You can learn Tangent Line by trying one small example instead of long theory."
        - paragraph: Find f(a). Find f'(a). Use point-slope form with the derivative as slope. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
        - paragraph: "In real life, road grade: Local slope of a path. Watch out: Using two far points for a tangent slope. Use the derivative at the tangent point."

      - article:
        - generic: "4"
        - heading "Understand" [level=3]
        - paragraph: "Tangent line models local behaviour: it matches the function’s value and slope at P."
      - article:
        - heading "Key Rule" [level=3]
        - paragraph: "For a differentiable function f at x = a:"
        - status: y − f(a) = f′(a) (x − a)
        - paragraph: This is the equation of the tangent line to y=f(x) at (a,f(a)).
        - generic: ♙ The tangent line is the limit of secant lines as two points on the curve come infinitely close.
      - article:
        - heading "Worked Example" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Find the tangent line to f(x)=x²−2 at x=−1.
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "1"
          - text: f(−1)=(−1)²−2=−1
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "2"
          - text: f′(x)=2x ⇒ f′(−1)=−2
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "3"
          - text: Use y−f(a)=f′(a)(x−a)
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "4"
          - text: y−(−1)=(−2)(x−(−1))
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "5"
          - text: y+1=−2(x+1)
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "6"
          - text: y=−2x−3
        - text: "Tangent line: y = −2x − 3"
      - article:
        - heading "Common Misconception" [level=3]:
          - text: Common Misconception
        - paragraph: Not every line through P is a tangent. Only one line has slope f′(a).
        - paragraph: Many lines pass through P, but only one matches the curve’s instantaneous slope.
